newsitem.title: INDIA: Daimler-Benz to raise stake in India unit.
newsitem.headline: Daimler-Benz to raise stake in India unit.

text.p: Mercedes-Benz India Ltd on Monday said its German parent Daimler-Benz AG plans to raise its share capital in the Indian firm assembling Mercedes luxury cars.

It said Tata Engineering and Locomotive Company Ltd (TELCO), its Indian partner owning 49 percent of Mercedes-Benz India, welcomed the firm's plan to raise exports and boost local Indian component suppliers.

"This programme may necessitate a further infusion of funds. In view of TELCO's investment commitments to its own business growth, it has been agreed between the partners that TELCO would not participate in the current capital increase," it said.
"Daimler-Benz's share is proposed to be enhanced. Nevertheless, Daimler-Benz recognises the local expertise of TELCO in key areas."
The statement did not say to what extent Daimler-Benz would raise its equity from its current holding of 51 percent.
Automobile sources said the German firm planned to raise its ownership to about 75 percent. Officials of Mercedes-Benz India were not available for comment.
"TELCO retains the option to subscribe to future equity share capital increases and maintain its shareholding percentage," the statement added.
The change in equity structure is subject to various government approvals, it said.
Mercedes-Benz is moving its factory to a newly-designed and TELCO-constructed plant at Chikhali, near the TELCO plant, in the western city of Pune.
